sections.html:
Delaware County deeds are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds in the Government Center, Room 108, 201 W. Front Street, Media, PA 19063. Real property records go back to 1789, the year the county was created from part of Chester County. The phone is 610-891-4152.

The counter is open from 8:30am to 4:30pm, but documents are taken for recording only from 8:30am to 3:30pm. If your closing runs late in the day, ask the title company how the deed will get in before the cutoff, since e-recording and hand delivery follow the same window.

One office handles every deed, but each deed also touches a municipality. The recorder collects the local share of transfer tax for the township, borough or city where the house sits, so the municipality named on the deed shapes your final bill.

Recording a four-page deed costs $117.25 under the fee schedule dated December 1, 2025. The $38.00 base fee covers up to four pages, four names and ten folio numbers, and county and state add-on charges make up the rest.

Delaware County recording fees for a four-page document
Document typeTotal fee
Deed$117.25
Mortgage$115.25
Satisfaction, release or assignment$84.25
Agreement, power of attorney or general miscellaneous$43.00
Certification (4 pages)$7.00

The deed total breaks down as follows.

  • Base fee: $38.00
  • County Affordable Housing charge: $18.00
  • Judicial computer, access to justice and criminal justice add-on: $41.25, which rose by $1.00 on December 1, 2025
  • County Improvement Fund: $5.00
  • Demolition of Blighted Properties charge: $15.00

Extra pages on a deed are $4.00 each, and every name after the fourth or folio after the tenth adds $1.00. Military discharge papers are recorded free.

Most Delaware County sales carry 2% in realty transfer tax: 1% to the state and 1% to the local taxing bodies. A few places charge more, so the municipality printed on your deed decides the rate.

  • Radnor Township: local 1.5%
  • Upper Darby Township: local 1.5%
  • Chester City: local 1.5%
  • Upper Providence Township: local 2%
  • Everywhere else in the county: local 1%

Contracts often split the tax between buyer and seller, so read the agreement of sale before assuming who writes the check. A seller in a 1.5% township pays noticeably more than one across the line in a 1% township, so check the municipality before you price an offer.

When a deed covers land in more than one municipality, it has to show what share of the value belongs to each taxing body, using the Pennsylvania Statement of Value.

For an in-person recording the office asks for three separate checks. Each has its own payee, and a single combined check gets the package returned.

  • One check for the recording fee, made out to Recorder of Deeds
  • One check for state transfer tax, made out to Recorder of Deeds, Agent
  • One check for local transfer tax, also made out to Recorder of Deeds, Agent

Every page needs a 1-inch top margin so the office can stamp recording data electronically without covering text. All documents are also subject to Solicitor approval before recording, so build that into the closing timeline.

E-recording submitters can flag incorrect fees until 11:30am on the next business day after a month ends. The office does not run title searches, so title work stays with the title company or an attorney.

The recorder's 2026-27 Common Level Ratio factor is 1.83. It applies to any document dated July 1, 2026 or later.

The ratio changes every fiscal year, so a deed dated before July 1, 2026 uses the earlier factor. If your document needs the factor at all, ask the office which one fits the date on your deed.

Records from 1799 to the present can be viewed online through the county's public access site, and copies cost less there than at the counter. Online copies are $0.50 per page; counter copies are $1.00 per page. Electronic certified copies are $12.50 through the public access site, while paper certifications are $7.00 for four pages plus $1.00 for each added page.

  • Property Alert: a free service that emails you when a document is recorded against your Property ID number
  • Return envelope: add $1.00 to a mailed request if you do not enclose one
  • Microfiche copies: $1.00 per page

Homeowners worried about deed fraud can sign up for Property Alert before listing. It costs nothing and shows quickly if someone records a document against the parcel.

The county's estimated population was 580,937 in July 2025, with 230,160 housing units. The median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $332,200, owner-occupancy is 69.6%, median gross rent is $1,372 and median household income is $89,546. The county issued 217 building permits for 2025.

At that price level, transfer tax is a real number in a sale here, so work out your municipality's rate before you pick a net-proceeds figure.

sections.h2: What the recorder will not do
sections.html:
The office records, indexes and reproduces documents. It does not search title, and it does not tell you which transfer tax rate your contract should assume. Those questions belong to your title company, attorney or the municipality involved.

Mistakes are expensive in time more than money. A deed returned for a missing margin, a wrong payee or a bad notary block has to be fixed and brought back inside the recording window, which closes at 3:30pm. If that slips past the cutoff, recording can slide to the next business day, and the buyer may be waiting on keys or funds.

Questions about a particular deed are best asked before the closing date. Phone 610-891-4152 and have the municipality, the parcel's Property ID number and the page count ready.

Ask your title company who will bring the deed and whether it will be e-recorded or delivered by hand before the 3:30pm cutoff. Confirm the municipality on the deed and the local rate that goes with it. Make sure three checks are ready, with the right payees, and that each page of the deed has its top margin.

If the sale is to a cash buyer, the recording steps are the same. The deed, the fee and the transfer tax still go to Room 108, and the new owner appears in the records once the office has indexed the document.

faqs.q: What is the cost to record a deed in Delaware County?
faqs.a: A four-page deed costs $117.25 under the December 1, 2025 schedule. Extra pages are $4.00 each, and names after four or folio numbers after ten add $1.00 each.

faqs.q: What are the transfer tax rates in Delaware County?
faqs.a: The standard rate is 1% state plus 1% local. Radnor, Upper Darby and Chester City charge 1.5% locally, and Upper Providence charges 2% locally.

faqs.q: What hours does the Delaware County Recorder of Deeds accept recordings?
faqs.a: Recording hours are 8:30am to 3:30pm, although the office stays open to 4:30pm. It is in Room 108 of the Government Center in Media.

faqs.q: Do I need separate checks to record a deed in Delaware County?
faqs.a: Yes. The office asks for one check for the recording fee, one for state transfer tax and one for local transfer tax. Tax checks go to Recorder of Deeds, Agent.

faqs.q: Can I look up Delaware County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes. Records from 1799 to the present are available online, with copies at $0.50 per page. Copies bought in the office are $1.00 per page.
